stories.title: WSO2 releases open control plane for governing enterprise AI agents
stories.summary: WSO2 says Agent Manager is now generally available as an open-source control plane for agents running across frameworks, models, and deployment environments. The release combines sandboxed execution, verifiable agent identity, MCP-level governance, OpenTelemetry tracing, evaluations, and lifecycle controls, with self-hosted or managed-SaaS deployment. For enterprise teams, the practical signal is that agent inventory, permissions, observability, and intervention are becoming a distinct operational layer rather than features left inside individual application projects.

stories.title: Anthropic maps a shift toward more autonomous AI-enabled cyberattacks
stories.summary: Anthropic’s review of 832 accounts banned for malicious cyber activity finds that attackers are using AI increasingly deeper in the attack lifecycle, including account discovery and other post-compromise work. The report says AI can chain attack stages, make tactical decisions, and execute with limited human intervention, while the MITRE ATT&CK framework does not yet represent that agentic orchestration well. Defenders therefore need to monitor sequences and autonomy, not only count isolated techniques or judge risk from the attacker’s apparent skill.

stories.title: AWS open-sources Pizza Bot, an inbox for background AI-agent work
stories.summary: AWS has released Pizza Bot, an Apache-2.0 open-source application that lets agents run in the background and return completed work or permission requests to an inbox. It is self-hosted, stores threads and state locally, supports several hosted model providers plus Ollama, and connects to MCP servers and the DeepAgents/LangGraph runtime. The project makes review queues and human approval part of the agent interface, while its community-project status means operators remain responsible for uptime, backups, updates, and the security of enabled tools.
